content.title: Valero Texas Open: J.J. Spaun captures third PGA Tour title
content.text: Updated April 5, 2026, 6:41 p.m. ETThe 2026 Valero Texas Open has been impacted by poor weather, including a suspension of the third round.The winner of the tournament could earn an invitation to the Masters if not already qualified.Due to heavy rain, golfers will play with preferred lies for the final round.SAN ANTONIO — Four years ago, J.J. Spaun captured the Valero Texas Open and earned his first Masters start in the process. This time around, Spaun already had a place in the Augusta field wrapped up, but the victory was just as special.After posting a breakout season in 2025, Spaun has struggled to start the 2026 campaign, missing the cut in four of his seven starts before coming back to the Alamo City.But with an eagle on the risk-reward 17th hole at TPC San Antonio’s Oaks Course and a crafty par on the final hole, Spaun notched his third PGA Tour victory on Sunday and will now head into major season with a huge boost of confidence.Spaun was one of seven players to share the lead on Sunday, but he held the lead when it mattered most: At the conclusion.Here are the highlights from the final round of the Valero Texas Open.2026 Valero Texas Open leaderboardCheck tee times and keep tabs on every score carded at TPC San Antonio with the 2026 Valero Texas Open live leaderboard.As of 5:22 p.m. ET, here was the scoreboard:PositionPlayerScore1J.J. Spaun−17T2Matt Wallace−16T2Michael Kim−164Andrew Putnam−15T5Robert MacIntyre−14T5Kevin Yu−14T5Ryu Hisatsune−14 Preferred lies are in effectAfter heavy rains waterlogged the course, this is one of the few instances in which there should be no one against preferred lies. Understandably, that will be the case for the final round of play.The last group of Robert MacIntyre and Ludvig Aberg started their final round at 12:01 p.m. local time. Valero Texas Open Sunday weather forecastThis course is already drenched, but there's even more rain on the way today, according to the National Weather Service. Here's the radar as of 9:27 a.m. local time (10:27 ET):It's much chillier here now to finish the week, and the temperature has not hit 60 yet this afternoon.Sunday's forecast calls for another soggy day in San Antonio. There's at least a 60 percent chance of rain from midnight until 1 p.m. local time, meaning the weather could again have a major impact on the Valero Texas Open. J.J. Spaun makes huge eagle to take lead on No. 17J.J. Spaun has won here before, and he looked like a reigning champion the way he handled the pressure on the 17th hole. Down a stroke, Spaun hit a great drive on the risk-reward par-4 and then buried an eagle putt to take the solo lead late in the day. Matt Wallace birdies three straight, takes leadAfter an opening-round 71, Matt Wallace has found his groove at the Valero Texas Open, and while the conditions are wet and chilly, Wallace is heating up at the right time.After chipping for birdie on No. 15, Wallace holed birdie putts on both No. 16 and No. 17 to take the solo lead (as of 2:40 p.m. local time) at TPC San Antonio. He sits at 16 under. Muddy dogfight as players near the turnThis is shaping up as a wild, sloppy finish as 14 players are within four shots of the lead at 3 p.m. ET, and the conditions will favor a mudder coming home.J.J. Spaun, who won here in 2022, made birdie on No. 10 and is now part of a six-way tie for the lead, as of 2:05 p.m. local time.Matt Wallace got into that scrum when he chipped in on 15th hole for birdie, then put his head in his hands as he clearly realized that had the ball not gone in the hole, it would have run well past.And Wallace isn't the only one who has chipped in today; Aberg did it on two separate occasions. Rain is coming down hard, as of 2:45 p.m. ETThe rain has increased this afternoon as storms roll through the area. Although play has yet to stop, and no lightning is in the region, the conditions are trying for certain. MacIntyre drops shot on 18, finishes third round with 72After pushing his second shot into a tough spot, Robert MacIntyre made bogey on the final hole of his third round late Sunday morning, meaning his lead was down to one as players move into their final round of play at TPC San Antonio. He'll start his final round at 12:01 p.m. local time at 14 under.MacIntyre's 72 let the field back in after his 66 and 64 in the opening two rounds gave an appearance that the Scotsman might run away with the tournament.Although MacIntyre technically has two victories on the PGA Tour, he's never won in the United States, as those wins came at the RBC Canadian and Genesis Scottish Open, both in 2024. Ludvig Aberg gets into lead, becomes betting favoriteWith a birdie on the second hole, Ludvig Aberg moved into a crowd five-way tie for the lead as of 1:50 p.m. ET, and Bet MGM pushed him into the role of betting favorite. As of that time, Aberg was installed as a +110 favorite with both Ryo Hisatsune (+400) in second and MacIntyre (+450) in third.Aberg has a pair of PGA Tour victories, but it's been over a year since he captured the 2025 Genesis Invitational.UPDATE: Aberg added a birdie on the third hole to get to 15 under and take the solo lead. Matt Wallace jumped near the topAfter finishing up a scintillating 64 in the third round at the Valero Texas Open, Matt Wallace birdied the second hole in his final round and has pulled into a tie for second place at 13 under as of 10:50 a.m. local time. He had moved into tie for the lead by the time he made the turn, posting a 2-under 34 on the front that had him at 14 under.Wallace, who has one Tour victory at the 2023 Corales Puntacana Championship, has not cracked inside the top 40 in any of his six starts this season. Sergio Garcia isn't here, but his tees still areTPC San Antonio's Oaks Course was designed by Greg Norman, in consultation with Sergio Garcia. When Norman was working through the project, Garcia was dating his daughter, Morgan-Leigh Norman. The two split up, however, before TPC San Antonio officially opened in 2010.According to the urban legend told by members, Garcia was not extensively involved as the project neared completion, but one of his major contributions to the course was an alternate tee box on 16, which is still rudimentarily maintained, but never set up for live play.The Sergio tees play over a pond (immaterial for Tour players) and a series of bunkers. It makes the hole considerably more difficult, even if it shortens things a bit.Here's more on the tee box, which those on the grounds might not even notice as they're following players. Ryo Hisatsune gulping way to topRegardless of his finish, it's been another great week for Ryo Hisatsune, who entered the final round of play T-2, but then used a birdie on the first hole to jump into a tie for the lead at 14 under.Hisatsune’s claim to fame is that he has the unusual habit of taking a gulp of water before every putt and any shot within 70 yards. Asked why he does it, he joked that he’s doing sake bombs and getting drunk. The real reason? To control nerves and calm himself down. Hey, don't knock it until you've tried it.Here are four other things to know about Hisatsune, who is seeking to become the sixth different player from Japan to win on the PGA Tour. Final round tee timesThe third round was officially completed at 11:15 a.m. CT. at TPC San Antonio, and here are the tee times for the final round with groups continuing play to try to finish by Sunday night.Watch PGA Tour Live on ESPN+Who leads the Valero Texas Open?Robert MacIntyre held a two-shot lead at 15 under when play was suspended just before 1 p.m. ET on Saturday. MacIntyre finished six holes in his third round and was 1 under for the day. Ludvig Aberg sat in solo second overnight at 13 under, one shot clear of a tie for third between Matt Wallace and Ryo Hisatsune.What's the total purse for the 2026 Valero Texas Open?The total purse for the 2026 Valero Texas Open is $9.8 million. The winner will pocket $1.764 million, or 20 percent of the total purse. See the full payouts here.
